subject: Post-demo: recommended inference shortlist, latency/cost estimates, and next actions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@avadata.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & recommended inference shortlist + next steps

Claire — thank you for the time today. Quick recap and a recommended shortlist based on the demo and the sample traffic profile you shared. I tried to balance quality, p95 latency, and run cost for the production mix (mix of short completion <64 tokens and episodic long answers ~400 tokens).

Recommended shortlist (primary -> fallback):
- Model A (quantized variant): highest quality for dialog and instruction-following; expected p95 single-request latency ~120ms on g4dn-like instance with Redwood batching; good KV reuse for conversational flows.
- Model B (optimized distilled): cost-forward option; p95 ~80ms, slightly lower long-form fidelity on edge cases; cheaper units/token.
- Model C (fallback smaller model): sub-50ms p95 for very low-latency endpoints; use for rate-limited bursts or degraded mode.

Attachments included: prompt set we used for demo (ava_prompt_set_v1.json) and the benchmark summary CSV. Benchmarks are from our internal run (links below) and reflect mixed batch sizes and your estimated concurrency.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Claire: confirm which route you want us to prioritize for the pilot (Model A primary or Model B primary).
2) Claire: any security questionnaire or PO cadence we should plan for? (you mentioned legal might want to review).
3) Redwood: we'll prepare a canary rollout plan and expected cost delta for 1M tokens/month for both Model A and Model B.
4) Internal (Karthik/Marissa/Dev): can you validate latency/cost numbers for the config below and flag any regression risks for Model A quantized variant?

Config assumptions used for numbers in the CSV:
- VM class: 1 x A10g-equivalent with burst pool; batching target 50ms latency-SLO; token mix: 70% short, 30% long.
- Quantization: 4-bit for Model A, with Redwood's slow-start kernel.

Links: s3://redwood-benchmarks/ava/20270503/results.json and the prompt-set in the attachment.

Thanks — I can sync next week if that helps.

— Soojin

Thanks Soojin — helpful summary. A couple of clarifying items before we lock our pilot path: 

1) For Model A you list p95 ~120ms. Is that measured cold or with warm KV cache for a typical multi-turn flow? We are especially sensitive to first-turn latency when a user opens a session.
2) Cost: can you give a top-line $/1M tokens estimate for both Model A (quantized) and Model B (distilled) assuming our projected monthly volume ~8M tokens? I want a comparison that includes the expected batch/caching savings you mentioned.
3) Regresion risk: our security team will want to understand if quantization introduces hallucination risk for our enterprise prompts. Please cc our legal and infosec when you have the questionnaire.

We likely prefer higher quality for the initial pilot but need the tradeoffs spelled out. Tom and legal are on copy for procurement timeline.

Claire Huang
Head of Product, Ava Data
claire@avadata.io

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap & recommended inference shortlist + Claire questions (latency/cost/regression)

Soojin — see notes below for what we can share back quickly. Kept it tight so you can forward to Claire and legal.

1) Latency (p95) estimates — config: 1x A10g-equivalent, dynamic batching with Redwood 50ms target, KV cache enabled for multi-turns.
- Model A (quantized 4-bit): cold p95 ~280ms (first request, cold kernels + weight init), warm p95 ~140ms with effective KV reuse for multi-turn flows. We have observed ~15-25% variance depending on prompt prefix length.
- Model B (distilled FP16): cold p95 ~180ms, warm p95 ~85ms. Lower cold-start penalty because smaller weights and fewer kernel switches.
- Model C (small fallback): cold p95 ~90ms, warm p95 ~45ms.

Notes: cold measurements assume no pre-warmed pools. If we pre-warm a small canary pool (recommended for pilot), cold p95 for Model A drops to ~160-170ms.

2) Cost estimates ($ per 1M tokens) — assumptions: mixed token length, batch yield improvements ~1.7x vs naive single-request, KV cache hit-rate 40% on multi-turns. These are order-of-magnitude back-of-envelope numbers for proposal discussions: 
- Model A (quantized 4-bit): $320 per 1M tokens (includes infra, GPU hours amortized, and expected batching savings).
- Model B (distilled FP16): $210 per 1M tokens.
- Model C (small): $95 per 1M tokens.

Caveats: Model A cost assumes additional engineering time for quantization validation and slightly higher memory footprint management. If we need stricter latency SLOs (p95 <100ms), cost increases materially because of dedicated reserved capacity.

3) Regression/hallucination risk for quantization:
- Known risk: 4-bit quantization can increase subtle coherence or factuality regressions on low-frequency tokens and edge-case instructions. For instruction-following and structured outputs it can manifest as formatting glitches or occasional truncation.
- Mitigations: run a focused regression suite comparing base FP16 vs quantized outputs across ~300 representative prompts (we can use the attached prompt set as a starting point but recommend expanding with 50 enterprise-specific probes focusing on licensing/legal language, entities, and numeric precision).
- Monitoring: add a lightweight quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE-style where applicable, and semantic similarity + hallucination detectors) and set automated regression alerts for >2% delta on high-value prompt subsets.

Recommended next steps we can share with the customer:
- Pilot baseline: Model A primary with a small pre-warmed canary pool for the first 48 hours, Model B as a hot standby for read-heavy/low-cost bursts.
- QA: expand prompt set with the 50 enterprise legal probes and run a 300-prompt regression comparison.
- Cost/Timeline: Redwood will provide a detailed $/1M estimate and a 2-week canary plan.

If you want I can draft a one-page note to forward to Claire/legal with the above bullets.

— Karthik
